items.name: Child's Pose
items.description: A restful kneeling stretch for the back, hips and shoulders.
items.setup: Kneel on a mat with your big toes together and knees apart, then sit back toward your heels.
steps: Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead on the floor or on a cushion.
Keep your arms reaching forward or rest them by your sides.
Breathe slowly and let your back relax.
items.breathing: Breathe deeply into your back and sides.
mistakes: Forcing the hips down to the heels.
items.easier: Place a cushion between your heels and hips, or under your chest.
cautions: If kneeling is painful, use the Lying Figure-Four Stretch instead.

items.name: Standing Quad Stretch
items.description: Stretches the front of the thigh while standing – useful after squats, lunges and cardio.
items.setup: Stand tall next to a wall or chair and hold it with one hand.
steps: Bend your outside knee and bring your heel toward your glutes.
Hold your ankle or sock, keeping your knees side by side.
Gently tuck your tailbone under until you feel a stretch at the front of the thigh.
Hold, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and let the muscle relax a little more with each breath out.
mistakes: Pulling the heel hard into the glutes.
Letting the knee drift out to the side.
items.easier: Rest your foot on a chair seat behind you instead of holding it, or loop a towel around your ankle.
cautions: Stop if you feel knee pain, and hold the foot lower.

items.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
items.description: A seated stretch for the back of the thigh.
items.setup: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other bent, with the sole of that foot resting against the inner thigh of the straight leg.
steps: Sit tall and hinge forward from your hips over the straight leg.
Reach toward your shin or foot without rounding your back excessively.
Stop when you feel a gentle stretch along the back of the thigh.
Hold, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe out to ease slightly deeper as the muscle relaxes.
mistakes: Bouncing in and out of the position.
Rounding from the upper back instead of hinging at the hips.
items.easier: Bend the straight knee slightly, or loop a towel around the foot.
cautions: A stretch should feel mild to moderate, never sharp.

items.name: Lying Figure-Four Stretch
items.description: A gentle lying stretch for the glutes and outer hips.
items.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
steps: Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Lift the other foot off the floor and hold behind that thigh.
Gently draw both legs toward you until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and keep your shoulders and head relaxed on the floor.
mistakes: Letting the crossed foot go floppy.
items.easier: Keep the bottom foot on the floor.
cautions: Avoid pushing on the crossed knee if it causes discomfort.

items.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
items.description: Stretches the back of the shoulder by drawing one arm across your chest.
items.setup: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
steps: Bring one arm across your chest at shoulder height.
Hold it just above the elbow with your other hand.
Gently draw the arm closer to your chest.
Hold, then switch arms.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and keep your shoulders down.
mistakes: Pressing directly on the elbow joint.
items.easier: Hold the arm a little lower, below shoulder height.
cautions: Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

items.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
items.description: Stretches the back of the upper arm and the side of the upper back.
items.setup: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart and your shoulders relaxed.
steps: Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand reaches down toward your upper back.
Use your other hand to press the elbow back gently.
Keep your head upright and your ribs down.
Hold, then switch arms.
items.easier: Place your hand on your shoulder instead of reaching down your back.
cautions: Skip this stretch if raising your arm overhead is painful.

items.name: Clasped-Hands Chest Opener
items.description: Opens the front of the chest and shoulders – a helpful counterbalance to sitting and pushing exercises.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Clasp your hands behind your lower back, or hold a towel between them.
Draw your shoulder blades gently together.
Lift your chest and raise your hands slightly away from your back.
Hold while keeping your chin level.
items.easier: Hold a towel with your hands wider apart.
cautions: Keep the stretch gentle at the front of the shoulders.

items.name: Sphinx Stretch
items.description: A gentle back bend on your forearms that stretches the front of the body and mobilises the spine.
items.setup: Lie face down with your legs extended and your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
steps: Press your forearms down and gently lift your chest.
Keep your hips and legs relaxed on the floor.
Lengthen through the top of your head and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Hold, then lower down.
mistakes: Tilting the head back to look up.
items.easier: Place a cushion under your chest for a smaller bend.
cautions: Reduce or skip the lift if back bends cause discomfort.

items.name: Wall Calf Stretch
items.description: A classic stretch for the calf muscles, using a wall for support.
items.setup: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it at shoulder height.
steps: Step one foot back, keeping that leg straight and the heel down.
Bend your front knee and lean gently toward the wall.
Keep both feet pointing forward.
Hold, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and relax into the stretch.
mistakes: Bouncing in and out of the position.
cautions: Ease off if you feel pain at the back of the ankle.

items.name: Butterfly Stretch
items.description: A seated stretch for the inner thighs and hips.
items.setup: Sit tall on the floor with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling out to the sides.
steps: Hold your ankles or feet.
Sit tall, lengthening through your spine.
Hinge gently forward from the hips until you feel a stretch in the inner thighs.
Hold, keeping the movement gentle.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and let your knees relax with each breath out.
mistakes: Pushing the knees down with the hands.
items.easier: Move your feet further from your body, or sit on a cushion.

items.name: Lying Spinal Twist
items.description: A relaxing twist lying on your back that eases the lower back and hips.
items.setup: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides at shoulder height and your knees bent, feet on the floor.
steps: Let both knees lower slowly to one side.
Keep both shoulders resting on the floor.
Turn your head away from your knees if that is comfortable.
Hold, then bring the knees back up and switch sides.
mistakes: Forcing the knees to the floor.
items.easier: Place a cushion under your knees.
cautions: Move slowly into and out of the twist.

items.name: Downward Dog
items.description: An upside-down V position that stretches the backs of the legs and lengthens the spine and shoulders.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with your hands slightly ahead of your shoulders.
steps: Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs as much as is comfortable, keeping a slight bend if needed.
Press the floor away and let your head hang between your arms.
Hold, then lower your knees to rest.
mistakes: Rounding the back to straighten the legs.
Forcing the heels to the floor.
items.easier: Keep your knees bent and place your hands on a raised surface.
items.harder: Hold for longer, or slowly pedal the feet.
cautions: Rise slowly if you feel dizzy.
Use fists if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
items.description: Stretches the front of the hip, which can feel tight after long periods of sitting.
items.setup: Kneel on one knee on a mat with the other foot in front, both knees bent at about 90 degrees.
steps: Gently tuck your tailbone under and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Shift your hips slightly forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Keep your torso upright.
Hold, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly, easing a little deeper as you breathe out.
mistakes: Letting the front knee cave in.
items.easier: Place a cushion under the back knee and shift forward less.
items.harder: Raise the arm on the same side as the back knee overhead.

items.name: Standing Side Stretch
items.description: A simple overhead reach and side bend to stretch along the sides of the body.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Raise one arm overhead.
Lean gently to the opposite side, reaching up and over.
Keep your hips centred and both feet on the floor.
Hold, return to the centre, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe into the stretched side of your body.
mistakes: Leaning forward or backward instead of directly sideways.
items.easier: Rest your other hand on your hip for support.
cautions: Keep the bend gentle if you have back discomfort.
